_about: Shared safety rules for each kind of product. status: ok | ask_doctor | avoid. Vitamin and mineral rules follow the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets; herbal rules follow NIH NCCIH 'Herbs at a Glance'.

child.text: Within the safe daily limit for your age.

pregnant.text: Vitamins and minerals are fine in pregnancy within the safe daily limits. Tell your doctor you take it.

breastfeeding.text: Fine while breastfeeding within the safe daily limits.

iron.label: Iron

child.text: Children only need an iron supplement if a doctor found low iron. Too much iron is a common cause of poisoning in young children.

pregnant.text: Pregnancy raises your iron need to 27 mg a day, so iron is often advised. Follow your doctor's dose.

breastfeeding.text: Iron need while breastfeeding is 9-10 mg a day, lower than before pregnancy.

periods.yes: Girls and women who have periods need more iron (15 mg a day for ages 14-18, 18 mg for ages 19-50). Heavy periods raise the risk of low iron.
periods.no: Without periods your iron need is lower (8-11 mg a day), which food usually covers. Take an iron supplement only if a blood test showed low iron.

iron.male_adult: Men need only 8 mg of iron a day, which food usually covers. Take an iron supplement only if a blood test showed low iron.

child.text: This is a pregnancy supplement. It is not designed for children.

male.text: This is made for women who are planning a pregnancy, pregnant or breastfeeding. It is not designed for men.

female_not_pregnant.text: Prenatal vitamins are made for women planning a pregnancy, pregnant or breastfeeding. If none of these apply, a normal multivitamin usually fits better.

pregnant.text: Made for pregnancy. It gives the extra folic acid and iron you need.

child.text: Safety of this herbal product in children under 18 has not been established. Ask a doctor first.

pregnant.text: Safety in pregnancy has not been established. Ask your doctor before taking it.

breastfeeding.text: Safety while breastfeeding has not been established. Ask your doctor before taking it.

child.text: Melatonin is a hormone. For children's sleep problems, see a doctor before using it.

pregnant.text: There is not enough research on melatonin in pregnancy. Ask your doctor first.

breastfeeding.text: There is not enough research on melatonin while breastfeeding. Ask your doctor first.

child.text: Follow the children's dose on the pack, if one is given.

pregnant.text: Ask your doctor before taking this in pregnancy.

breastfeeding.text: Ask your doctor before taking this while breastfeeding.

all.text: This product is not a dietary supplement, so MediSafe cannot check it. Ask a pharmacist.
